subject: Next steps — embeddings model-fit & eval (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — embeddings model-fit & eval (post-call recap)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard:
- Primary use case: semantic search over product docs + changelogs (mix of short and long docs).
- Current baseline: all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings, ~768-dim; you mentioned recall@10 ~0.62 and MRR ~0.34.
- Main concerns: drift over time (docs updated weekly), dimensionality vs latency/cost tradeoffs, and avoiding quality regressions when we optimize for cost.

Proposed next steps (we can iterate):
1) Send a 1k-query eval set (or the closest labeled set you have) — preferred format: JSONL with {query_id, query, positive_doc_ids, negative_doc_ids}.
2) We run a model-fit evaluation across 3 embedding configs:
   - rwd-embed-512 (dense, 512-d) — balanced latency/cost
   - rwd-embed-768-quant (quantized 768-d) — higher recall potential, lower storage cost
   - SBERT/mpnet (all-mpnet-base-v2) — your current baseline for a direct comparison
   Metrics: Recall@K (1/5/10), MRR, NDCG@10, average cosine similarity on positives/negatives, inference latency p50/p95.
3) We'll share a short report + recommended model/config with estimated per-embedding cost and expected latency impact.
4) Optional: if you’re comfortable, we can run a rolling drift check on a weekly snapshot to surface regressions.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.pdf (proposed timeline), sample_eval_prompts.csv (example JSONL template).

Questions for you before we kick off:
- Can you share the eval JSONL or a 1k sample by EOD Thu (3/18)?
- Any security/compliance requirements (retention, KMS) we should surface before running data on Redwood test cluster?

Happy to align on a time for a follow-up to walk through the results. I’ll loop Marissa and Rachel on scheduling.

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI evaluation team <ml-eval@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — embeddings model-fit & eval (post-call recap)

Thanks Marcus — this is super helpful.

I pulled together our current baseline artifacts and a small sample: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_acme_benchmarks (you should have view access). Quick baseline numbers from our internal eval runner: recall@10 = 0.62, MRR = 0.34 (1k holdout). As you noted, we use all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-d) today.

We can produce the JSONL you requested — we have a 1k labeled set but need to scrub some PII first. Will aim to share a redacted version by EOD Thu (3/18).

Two items to flag: 
- Drift: our docs update weekly and embeddings tend to degrade after ~6–8 weeks in our internal monitoring. Interested in automated drift checks.
- Security: need to confirm data retention and whether Redwood persists embeddings from eval runs. We’ll want the standard SOC2/KMS notes before we run anything with sensitive content.

Also looping in our eval team (ml-eval@acme.ai) to coordinate the JSONL output.

Best,
Alice Zhang
Head of Search & Relevance
Acme AI

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Acme AI evaluation team <ml-eval@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — embeddings model-fit & eval (post-call recap)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alice. That Drive link looks good.

For the JSONL format, here’s the minimum we need (we’ll accept CSV as well but JSONL is preferred):
{"query_id": "<string>", "query": "<text>", "positive_doc_ids": ["doc_123"], "negative_doc_ids": ["doc_456"]}

We’ll run the eval in our embed-eval harness and return: Recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, p50/p95 latency, and a short qualitative error analysis on samples where the baseline outperforms the candidate.

Security notes: we do not persist eval embeddings by default for short diagnostic runs — they’re ephemeral unless you opt into retention for monitoring. I’ll attach a short SOC2/KMS FAQ and a pointer to our compliance page during the run.

I’ve attached eval_template.jsonl (example) and re-attached the mutual action plan. If you can share the redacted JSONL by EOD Thu, we’ll queue the job and aim to deliver results within 24 hours.

Next steps:
- Alice / ml-eval: share JSONL (or confirm CSV)
- Marcus: run 3-config evaluation and share report + cost/latency estimate
- Marissa / Rachel: schedule 30–45m follow-up to review results and recommended config

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI evaluation team <ml-eval@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — embeddings model-fit & eval (post-call recap)

Thanks — 10:00am PT on Thu 3/18 works for us (please send invite). We’ll send a redacted 1k JSONL by EOD today.

Quick question to prep: could you include a short note in the report about dimensionality tradeoffs (512 vs 768) and quantization impact on recall vs latency/cost? Specifically interested in:
- Expected % change in recall@10 (ballpark) when moving 768->512 vs going 768->quantized 768
- Typical p95 latency delta per query for 512 vs 768 on GPU serving vs CPU (ballpark numbers are fine)
- Storage per million embeddings for dense 512 / dense 768 / quantized 768

If you can include those estimates in the evaluation report, that will help us with internal finance and infra planning.

Alice

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Acme AI evaluation team <ml-eval@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — embeddings model-fit & eval (post-call recap)

Perfect — thanks for the confirmation, Alice. We’ll run the evaluation as soon as we ingest the redacted JSONL and include the dimensionality/quantization ballpark estimates in the report. High-level notes we’ll include before the call: 
- Recall delta estimates (very rough): 768 -> 512: expect a small drop in recall@10 (~3–7% absolute depending on task); 768 dense -> 768 quantized: often <2–4% depending on quantization scheme, with material storage savings.
- Latency (p95) ballpark on our infra: CPU serving (optimized): 512 ~ 8–12ms, 768 ~ 12–18ms; GPU serving: 512 ~ 2–4ms, 768 ~ 3–5ms (these vary with batching).
- Storage per 1M embeddings (approx): dense 512 (float32) ~ 2 GB; dense 768 ~ 3 GB; quantized 768 (8-bit) ~ 0.75–1 GB.

We’ll validate these in the report with exact numbers from the run. See you on the call at 10am PT.

Best,
Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
